= Repository rulesets

[IMPORTANT]
====
**GitHub does not read this directory.** Unlike `.github/workflows/`,
`.github/dependabot.yml` or `.github/settings.yml`, ruleset JSON in a repository
path is *not* auto-applied by any GitHub feature. These files are
**documentation of intent plus a ready-to-POST payload** — nothing more.

A ruleset only takes effect once someone applies it via the REST API or imports
it in the web UI. Until then the protection described here **is not in force**.
====

== Applying a ruleset

Per ADR-0003 the *Configure* stage is an operator stage: identity, visibility and
branch/tag protection are set out of band. Automation is future work and must not
be described as existing.

[source,bash]
----
# Apply (create) a ruleset on the current repo:
gh api --method POST \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets" \
  --input .github/rulesets/tag-protection.json

# List what is actually in force — the only authoritative answer:
gh api "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets" --jq '.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.name)\t\(.enforcement)"'

# Update an existing ruleset in place (needs its numeric id from the list above):
gh api --method PUT \
  "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/<id>" \
  --input .github/rulesets/tag-protection.json
----

== Files

`tag-protection.json`:: Makes release tags immutable — blocks tag creation,
update and deletion, and requires signed tags. `bypass_actors` grants the
repository *admin* role (`actor_id: 5`) an always-bypass, so a maintainer can
still cut a release.

== Verifying

Do not infer that a ruleset is active because the JSON is present. Check with the
`gh api ... /rulesets` list above. A ruleset that exists as a file but was never
POSTed is the tag-protection equivalent of a check that cannot fail.
